newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech bank IPB says cancels GDR issue.
newsitem.headline: Czech bank IPB says cancels GDR issue.

text.p: Czech bank IPB a.s. said on Friday it was cancelling its planned Global Depositary Receipt (GDR) issue to avoid a clash with government plans to sell its stake in the bank to a foreign strategic investor.

The bank said in a statement that another reason for the cancellation was higher-than expected interest of current shareholders in the first round of its equity expansion scheme, leaving little left over for the GDR plan.

Earlier in the day, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said he planned to submit a proposal for IPB's full privatisation as well as the selloff of state shares in other three of the so- called "Big Four" Czech banks to cabinet within 14 days.

"Considering that this (governemnt) interest would clash with the IPB GDR programme, and that significantly higher-than expected subscription was reached in the first round of the new share issue, the supervisory board agreed to close off the new issue on the level reached in the first round," IPB said.
IPB said it had information the state planned to sell its stake in the bank to a "significant foreign strategic partner as a pilot project of full privatisation of large Czech banks."

Kocarnik was quoted by the Czech agency CTK as saying that his plan, which must be approved by the cabinet, would privatise the remaining state shares in IPB first, and foreign investors would be eligible to participate.

IPB said earlier this month it was at least delaying the GDR issue due to poor timing because of questions of stability in the Czech banking sector and strong demand for its earlier domstic rights issue.

The bank's shareholders approved an equity expansion earlier this year of 1.5 billion crowns of which 1.15 billion was subscribed by existing shareholders in the first round of a domestic rights issue.
The remainder was originally planned to comprise the GDR issue, lead-managed by Nomura.
IPB said in the statement that after the rights issue its basic capital totals 5.68 billion crowns of which the state-run National Property Fund (FNM) holds a 31.5 percent stake.
